findings.evidence: Lines 439–443 conclude `Bornology.IsBounded ... ∧ IntervalIntegrable ... ∧ ...`; repository/Mathlib grep finds no declaration using `isBdd`, while the naming conventions require names to describe conclusions in standard terminology.
findings.fix: Rename the prefix to `isBounded_intervalIntegrable_...`, preserving the standard predicate names appearing in the conclusion.
findings.issue: `isBddIntegrable_windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed_of_interior_crossings` compresses two distinct conclusions into the nonstandard term `isBddIntegrable`; `Bdd` has no relevant Mathlib precedent and `Integrable` fails to identify `IntervalIntegrable`.

findings.evidence: Both declarations take base/window and concatenation constructors before proving `Q` for arbitrary intervals; the naming-conventions section on induction principles requires `induction` when the motive eliminates into `Prop`.
findings.fix: Rename them with `induction` names describing their domains, such as `piecewise_induction` and `sorted_crossing_induction`.
findings.issue: `piecewise_gluing_aux` describes implementation machinery, and `sorted_crossing_gluing_aux` at `Crossing/PVAggregation.lean:121` has the same problem; both are public induction principles over a `Prop`-valued motive `Q`.

summary: Public names use nonstandard abbreviations and describe proof machinery instead of the structural induction principles provided.
